cases.question: Under MDR Article 83(1)-(2), what must a manufacturer's post-market surveillance system do, and how often must class IIa versus class IIb and III manufacturers update their PSUR under Article 86(1)?
cases.single_chunk_assessment: Neither cited chunk contains the full specified Article 83(2) system function and both Article 86 update frequencies; other equivalent support has not been exhaustively adjudicated.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Risk- and type-appropriate system integrated with quality management

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: For each device, manufacturers shall plan, establish, document, implement, maintain and update a post-market surveillance system in a manner that is proportionate to the risk class and appropriate for the type of device.
That system shall be an integral part of the manufacturer's quality management system referred to in Article 10(9).

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Systematic lifetime data, conclusions and preventive and corrective action

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: The post-market surveillance system shall be suited to actively and systematically gathering, recording and analysing relevant data on the quality, performance and safety of a device throughout its entire lifetime, and to drawing the necessary conclusions and to determining, implementing and monitoring any preventive and corrective actions.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Class IIb and III at least annually

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: Manufacturers of class IIb and class III devices shall update the PSUR at least annually.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Class IIa when necessary and at least every two years

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: Manufacturers of class IIa devices shall update the PSUR when necessary and at least every two years.

cases.question: For an imported MDR device, what importer identification details and locations are specified in Article 13(3), and which distributor checks may use representative sampling under Article 14(2)?
cases.single_chunk_assessment: The two cited MDR chunks are complementary. Dual-applicable MDCG 2021-27 chunk da229a705fe07e95a08d6787110535761003590fba1c14eb3a9b0a287ceee4a7 covers sampling and importer information generally; review its full context and other guidance before excluding a single-chunk alternative.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Importer identification details and permitted locations

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: Importers shall indicate on the device or on its packaging or in a document accompanying the device their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, their registered place of business and the address at which they can be contacted, so that their location can be established.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Additional label must not obscure manufacturer information

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: They shall ensure that any additional label does not obscure any information on the label provided by the manufacturer.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Representative sampling permitted for points (a), (b), and (d)

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: In order to meet the requirements referred to in points (a), (b) and (d) of the first subparagraph the distributor may apply a sampling method that is representative of the devices supplied by that distributor.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Point (a): CE marking and declaration

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: (a) the device has been CE marked and that the EU declaration of conformity of the device has been drawn up;

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Point (b): manufacturer information

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: (b) the device is accompanied by the information to be supplied by the manufacturer in accordance with Article 10(11);

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Point (d): UDI where applicable

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: (d) that, where applicable, a UDI has been assigned by the manufacturer.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Point (c) is not included in the express sampling permission

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: (c) for imported devices, the importer has complied with the requirements set out in Article 13(3);

In order to meet the requirements referred to in points (a), (b) and (d) of the first subparagraph the distributor may apply a sampling method that is representative of the devices supplied by that distributor.

guidance_excerpt.exact_quote: For distributors, a sampling method representative of the devices supplied can be used to verify information in Article 14(2) (a), (b) and (d) of the Regulations.

alternative_adjudication.finding: Guidance alone omits the specific Article 13(3) importer identification fields and no-obscuring qualification. Paired with Article 13(3), it identifies the sampling points and describes device information generally but does not explicitly state that the distributor checks the declaration has been drawn up. It is not verified complete for this rubric; other alternatives remain unreviewed.

cases.question: According to Q4’s Table 1 in the Annex XVI transition Q&A, what transition end date and two conditions applying throughout the period are listed? Separately, according to Q10, how must a dual-purpose device handle applicable MDR and common-specification requirements when they differ?
cases.single_chunk_assessment: Table 1 and Q10 provide complementary substantive elements; the source-specific question establishes which table and Q&A are requested.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Table 1 transition end date: 31 December 2029
Prior lawful Union marketing and continuing compliance

supporting_excerpts.locator: Q4 Table 1, page 4, first condition cell
supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: the product was lawfully marketed in the Union before 22 June 2023 and continues to comply with the requirements of Union and national law that were applicable to it before 22 June 2023;

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: No significant changes in design and intended purpose

supporting_excerpts.locator: Q4 Table 1, page 4, first condition cell
supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: the manufacturer does not make significant changes in the design and intended purpose of the product.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Dual-purpose requirements apply cumulatively

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: For a dual-purpose device, which has both a medical and a non-medical intended purpose, the applicable requirements from MDR and CS must be cumulatively fulfilled.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Stricter requirement where requirements differ

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: Considering that the device must fulfil both the applicable requirements from the MDR and the CS, in case such requirements differ, for example in setting the end of the transitional period, the stricter requirement should be taken into consideration and fulfilled.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Other dated conditions apply; the two ongoing conditions are not a complete product-eligibility assessment

supporting_excerpts.locator: Q4 Table 1, page 4, dated condition cell
supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: the sponsor has started the clinical investigation

alternative_adjudication.decision: User approved Table 1 plus Q10 as the substantive complete combination for the source-specific question. Q4 introductory text is supporting context only. Other combinations remain unjudged.
alternative_adjudication.structured_table: Page 4 Table 1: header 22/06/2023 to 31/12/2029; first row first cell contains both ongoing conditions; three dates in the next row align with condition cells in the following row. Relationships checked in structured table.

cases.question: According to MDCG 2024-13, how does the regulatory treatment of ethylene oxide used during manufacture of a sterile medical device differ from that of ethylene-oxide cartridges used by a health institution to sterilise reusable medical devices?
cases.single_chunk_assessment: The section 2.1 opening supplies additional QMS context but is not required for the substantive rubric. The continuation and section 2.2 are the approved substantive combination; the disclaimer is separately scored during answer review.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Manufacturing use in MDR/IVDR scope, EtO itself not device/accessory for that use, BPR exclusion

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: That means that this use of EtO is in scope of the MDR and IVDR even though EtO does not itself fall under the definitions of medical device or accessory for a medical device if used during the manufacturing process.

Therefore, EtO falls outside the scope of the BPR, as its Article 2(2)(b) provides that the BPR does not apply in case of biocidal products or treated articles falling within the scope of the MDR or IVDR.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Process and validation controlled, device conformity assessment, no extra assessment of EtO itself

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: Where EtO is used for sterilisation during the manufacturing of medical devices and IVDs, its use is controlled as part of the sterilisation and validation processes of the manufacturer.
These processes are subject to MDR/IVDR conformity assessment procedure in relation to the device being sterilised.
EtO itself is not subject to additional MDR/IVDR conformity assessments.

mandatory_element_evidence.summary: Specified health-institution cartridge use in MDR scope and outside BPR

supporting_excerpts.exact_quote: EtO and the associated sterilising equipment can also be used by health institutions for sterilisation before first use of medical devices or after their use to enable their re-use.

In this case the EtO cartridges used for the sterilisation are in scope of the MDR by virtue of falling under the definition of medical device, or accessory for a medical device, and therefore are outside the scope of the BPR as per Article 2(2)(b) BPR.
